definition: The final project at the end of the certificate that brings together all prior learning on a data-analytics scenario; on Coursera it is called the capstone, in hiring outside the classroom the same work is more often called a case study.

A practice data-analytics project with a title, problem statement, goals and deliverables, and a dataset, commonly used by employers under a time limit to assess how a candidate approaches a data problem.
A curated collection of case studies and project samples hosted publicly, for example on GitHub, Kaggle, Tableau, or a personal blog, and linked from a resume to showcase skills to employers.
The set of components to include in a portfolio: concise biography, contact page, resume, career accomplishments, and an optional photo.

The set of sections to include in a case study: introduction stating purpose and assumptions, problems with supporting facts, solutions with alternatives and pros and cons, conclusion summarizing takeaways, and next steps recommending who should do what and when.

aliases: Working with Existing Questions and Datasets
definition: The capstone track that uses a given business task and dataset, such as the Cyclistic or Bellabeat packets, to demonstrate job skills for interviews by running a defined analysis to specified deliverables.

aliases: Choosing Your Own Questions and Dataset
definition: The capstone track that requires finding a public dataset on a topic of personal interest, creating the business task and audience, and producing a self-directed case study through the full data analysis process.

A portfolio published on a public host such as Kaggle, GitHub, Tableau Public, Medium, WordPress, or Google Sites, kept personal, simple, relevant, presentable, and unique with cited sources, and linked from professional profiles.
A short statement of a couple of sentences describing an idea or concept, condensed enough to explain to someone in an elevator.

A Google tool at grow.google/interview-warmup that helps analysts practice answering interview questions, transcribes responses in real time, and provides insights on talking points, most-used words, and job-related terms.
A type of AI that can generate new content, like text, images, or other media, based on a prompt.
Input that provides instructions to an AI tool about how to generate output.
